version_statement.version: v1.1: Edited data for public distribution
version_statement.version_notes:
Version 1: Contained data from January 1970  to May 2023. 

Version 1.1: Contains updated data, from January 1970  to June 2026. The following data files have been updated:

- cpi-2008-2017 and cpi-2017-2023 have been updated to cpi-2008-2026-v1.1
- cpi-average-prices-urban-2017-2023 has been updated to cpi-2017-2026-prices-urban-v1.1
- cpi-average-prices-2017-2023 has been updated to cpi-2017-2026-prices-provinces-v1.1

The cpi-2017-2026-5&8-digit-v1 is a new additional data file.

study_info.abstract:
The CPI is a current social and economic indicator constructed to measure changes over time in the general level of prices of consumer goods and services that households acquire, use, or pay for. The index measures changes in consumer prices over time by measuring the cost of purchasing a fixed basket of consumer goods and services of constant quality and similar characteristics. The products in the basket are selected to be representative of households' expenditure during a specific year. Such an index is called a fixed-basket price index. Changes in the index reflect the effects of price changes on the cost of achieving a constant standard of living.

The South African CPI has three equally important objectives: 
1. To measure inflation in the economy so that macroeconomic policy is based on comprehensive and up-to-date price information. 
2. To measure changes in the cost of living of South African households to promote equity in measures taken to adjust wages, grants, service agreements and contracts. 
3. To provide a deflator for consumer expenditure in the national accounts and other economic data, to compute volume (as opposed to nominal) estimates. 

In compiling the South African CPI, Stats SA largely follows the methodology guidelines in the 2020 Consumer Price Index Manual: Concepts and Methods published jointly by the International Monetary Fund, International Labour Organization, Statistical Office of the European Union, United Nations Economic Commission for Europe, Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, and World Bank.
study_info.notes:
The South African CPI uses the 1999 version of the Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose (COICOP) of the United Nations Statistical Division to classify goods and services. COICOP is the international standard for classifying household expenditure. Goods and services are classified according to their intended use. 

The high-level COICOP categories are: 

01 - Food and non-alcoholic beverages 
02 - Alcoholic beverages and tobacco 
03 - Clothing and footwear 
04 - Housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels 
05 - Furnishings, household equipment and routine household maintenance 
06 - Health 
07 - Transport 
08 - Communication 
09 - Recreation and culture 
10 - Education 
11 - Restaurants and hotels 
12 - Miscellaneous goods and services

analysis_info.data_appraisal: In the cpi-2017-2026-prices-provinces-v1.1 data file, there are no observations from April 2020 to May 2022. The previous version of this data file also had no observations in this time period.
